News highlights 26th November 2026

_LOCAL NEWS_🇱🇰
Sri Lanka spared as US targets major trading partners with new tariffs
Sri Lanka has been left out of the latest round of US tariff measures targeting several major trading partners, including China, India, the European Union (EU), Vietnam and Bangladesh. The new tariffs, announced by the White House following investigations into the trade practices of 14 economies, are set to affect some of the US’ biggest trading partners, with rates ranging from 20% to as high as 40%.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4d94mr2v

Sri Lanka opens Rs 161.5 m national battery testing centre
Sri Lanka has established its first comprehensive national facility for testing modern battery technologies, introducing specialised testing capabilities for local manufacturers, importers and technology developers through an investment of approximately Rs 161.5 million, under the patronage of the Science and Technology Minister Prof Chrishantha Abeysena, according to the Department of Government Information (DGI).
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/y5jn9hxc

SriLankan Airlines adds fuel surcharge to break even by March after $35mn first-half loss
SriLankan Airlines has added a small fuel surcharge to upcoming ticket sales in a bid to break even by March, after surging jet fuel prices pushed the national carrier to a 35 million US dollar loss in the first two quarters of the year, Deputy Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku said.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/uevkkv4s

Exports hit record $ 15.28 b in 10 months; October tops $ 1.62 b
Sri Lanka’s export earnings reached a record $ 15.28 billion in the first months of 2026, up 6.03% year-on-year (YoY), supported by strong merchandise and services performance, while October also delivered the highest monthly export revenue on record at over $ 1.62 billion.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/5ax92kwz

Port of Colombo eyes $ 2k-3k value addition per container
The Port of Colombo is seeking to increase the economic value generated from each container handled through its operations from the current $ 50-100 to as much as $ 2,000-3,000 by attracting a greater share of container traffic for domestic value-added activities, Deputy Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku said yesterday (25).
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/8krmb3x6

President presses for faster land release as 18-month wait deters investors
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has pressed for faster allocation of land to investors, saying tax concessions alone are not enough to attract investment while the process of obtaining land takes about 18 months, the Parliament Secretariat said.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/jf2de42z

Bilateral trade and investment: SL eyes RCEP through ASEAN door
Sri Lankan Ambassador to Indonesia Sashikala Premawardhane reiterated Sri Lanka’s intention to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) – through its work as an ASEAN Sectoral Dialogue Partner – during an interview with Indonesian media platform Good News from Indonesia, published yesterday (25).
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/y68fhjr7

_Global News_🌎
Trump unveils new tariffs over excess industrial capacity, undeterred by midterms defeat
US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan ​and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in US midterm elections.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4vjsx42m

Asia shares bounce, AI and tariffs lurk in background
Asian shares eked out a rare rally on Thursday after ​Wall Street fought back from deep lows, though concerns over the circular financing of AI and a new ‌round of US tariffs made for a muted mood in a holiday-thinned session.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/yzm7t6vx

The rate hike has reached the banks, not yet the borrowers

On 20 November, the CBSL raised the OPR by 25bps to 9.00% and the SRR to 3%. Banks have already pulled back on lending, but borrowers have not, and loan demand is still rising. Our analysis suggests 9.00% is likely the peak, with gradual cuts possible next year.
